page0.text:
"Stop it!
I'm begging you, don't do this here!"
Sakura's sobbing voice brings me back to my senses.

page1.text:
"Sakura..."
"Well, this is a surprise. I think this is the first time you've ever talked back to me."
Shinji's voice is filled with an amusement I've never heard from him before.
Sakura stares at the ground, slightly trembling.

page2.text:
"So what do you want to do, Sakura? Will you stay here or come home to the Matous? I'm a nice brother, so I'll respect your opinion."
"...I'll do what you say, so please don't do this in front of Senpai. I'll come home, I promise."

page3.text:
"You'll do what I say?"
"..."
Sakura nods wordlessly.

page4.text:
"Okay. Then I won't take you home. I'm a generous big brother, after all. I have to let you do what you want. Isn't that right, Emiya?"
"Shinji..."

page5.text:
"Haha. Why are you so mad? It was just a joke, man. I was giving you a hard time. People are gonna think you're some loser if you always hold a grudge."
Shinji returns to the door.

page6.text:
"Later, Emiya. Take care of Sakura.
...But Sakura, you can come home anytime you want."
He leaves with a wave.
Shinji departs the Emiya house without Sakura.

page7.text:
I resume making dinner.
"..."
I don't know what to talk about, so I just cut tomatoes and pumpkin.
The only sound in the kitchen is the chop-chop of knife on cutting board. This is awkward.

page8.text:
"Senpai, the rice is cooked. Ms. Fujimura isn't here yet, but should I start serving?"
"Uh...yeah. It's a little early, but let's do that."
"Okay. I'll get ready."

page9.text: Sakura moves briskly, helping me as if the earlier confrontation never happened.

page10.text:
...But it's obvious she's forcing herself to act that way.
Sakura's acting calm because she doesn't want me to worry.

page11.text:
"..."
If that's Sakura's choice, then I can only play along.
She's the one who's most troubled right now.
Even if it's a forced smile, I should still give her a smile of my own...huh?

page12.text:
"Sakura?"
I hear the sound of a bowl dropping, and turn.
...
A shattered rice bowl is at Sakura's feet.

page13.text:
...
"Guh...!"
She suddenly collapses.
The strength goes out of her legs, and she falls to her knees then backwards.

page14.text:
"Sakura!"
I rush over and support her.
"A fever!?"
It's bad.
I can feel Sakura's fever even through her uniform.

page15.text:
"Sakura... Hey, get it together!"
"Eh...? Sen...pai? What's...wrong...?"

page16.text:
Her voice is listless.
Even though she's on the verge of passing out, I can tell that she's doing her best to form words.

page17.text:
"You still haven't gotten over your cold, obviously!"
"Ah...no, but...I'm still okay..."
"You idiot! People don't pass out when they're 'okay'!"

page18.text:
Damn it, I'm such a fool.
How could I have let Sakura work hard all day when I knew she's still sick?
Throw in what happened earlier on top of that, and it's no surprise she'd faint from the mental and physical stress!

page19.text:
"More importantly, I'm sorry for breaking the bowl.
I'll clean it up—ahh!?"
I scoop Sakura up in my arms.

page20.text:
"S-Senpai!?"
"Dinner can wait. I'm going to tuck you into bed. I'll take any complaints once you get better."

page21.text:
I walk to the guesthouse carrying Sakura in my arms.
I ignore anything she tries to say along the way.
To be honest, I'm in such an intense mood that her words barely register, anyway.

page22.text:
...
After a while, Sakura takes the hint and stops protesting by the time we get to the guestroom.
She looks somber and does what I ask.
The fever appears to have worsened, though the rest of her body doesn't feel any warmer.

page23.text:
I leave the guestroom.
Time to change the dinner menu.
I need to hurry and make okayu and something to accompany it.

page24.text:
It's almost 10:00 PM.
Dinner is over, and it's time to get ready to go out on patrol.

page25.text:
"..."
Sakura is sleeping in her bedroom.
I ate dinner with Saber.
Fuji-nee didn't come over. Maybe she's busy.

page26.text:
"Shirou. It is about time."
"..."
Saber wants to head out.
Tonight, we'll...
